t.1.201.1: Nārada said: Listen from me, together with your brothers, O Pārtha Yudhiṣṭhira, to this ancient history in detail, just as it happened.
t.1.201.2: Long ago, in the lineage of the great Asura Hiraṇyakaśipu, there was a lord of the Daityas named Nikumbha, who was mighty and full of splendor.
t.1.201.3: To him were born two sons of great valor and fearsome prowess; they ate together with one another and never went anywhere without each other.
t.1.201.4: Each did what was pleasing to the other, each spoke kindly to the other; one in character and conduct, they were like a single being made into two.
t.1.201.5: Those two, grown to manhood and of great valor, of one mind even in all their undertakings, set their minds on a single resolve for the purpose of conquering the three worlds.
t.1.201.6: Having undertaken consecration, the two went to the Vindhya, and there they practised fierce austerity. And after a long time the two became endowed with the power of austerity.
t.1.201.7: Worn out by hunger and thirst, wearing matted locks and garments of bark, their whole bodies caked with dirt, the two of them came to live on air alone.
t.1.201.8: Offering their own flesh as oblations into the fire, standing on the tips of their great toes, with arms raised and eyes unblinking, the two held fast to their vows for a long time.
t.1.201.9: Scorched for a long time by the power of the austerities of those two, the Vindhya mountain gave forth smoke; that was like a wonder.
t.1.201.10: Then the gods became frightened, seeing the fierce austerity of those two, and so, to destroy their austerity, the gods created obstacles.
t.1.201.11: Again and again they tempted the two with jewels and with women, yet those two, firm in their very great vow, did not break their vow.
t.1.201.12: Then the gods once more cast an illusion upon those two great-souled ones: their sisters, their mothers, their wives, and likewise their retinue appeared before them.
t.1.201.14: Then all the women, running up to the two of them, cried out, "Save us!" But those two of exceedingly great vows did not break their vow.
t.1.201.13: Chased by a rakṣas with a spear in hand, they fled in terror, their ornaments and the locks of their hair loosened and their garments slipping from one side.
t.1.201.16: Then the Grandfather, the Grandfather of all the worlds, approached the two great Asuras in person and tempted them with the offer of a boon.
t.1.201.15: When neither of the two was shaken or distressed, then those women and the entire apparition vanished.
t.1.201.17: Then those two brothers, Sunda and Upasunda, firm in their valor, beholding the god, the Grandfather, stood there with joined palms.
t.1.201.18: Then the two of them, together, spoke to the lord god: "If the Grandfather is pleased with this austerity of ours,
t.1.201.19: If the lord is pleased with us, may we both be masters of magic and masters of weapons, mighty, able to take any form at will, and immortal.
t.1.201.22: You two have undertaken austerity for the sake of conquering the three worlds; for this reason, O lords of the Daityas, I do not grant your wish.
t.1.201.20: Except for immortality, everything else you two have asked for shall be yours. Let something else be chosen instead: a safeguard against death that will make you equal to the immortals.
t.1.201.21: Because this great austerity was undertaken by you two with the thought, 'We two shall accomplish this,' for that reason immortality is not granted to you.
t.1.201.24: What you two have asked for, just as it was spoken, this wish I grant to you both; and this ordinance concerning death shall be for you two exactly as you desired.
t.1.201.23: Whatever being there is in the three worlds, whether moving or unmoving, from all of it let there be no fear for us two, except from each other, O Grandsire.
t.1.201.25: Then the Grandsire, having granted this boon to the two of them and having turned them back from their austerities, went to the world of Brahmā.
t.1.201.26: Having obtained all the boons, those two lords of the Daityas, both of them unslayable by all the world, went back to their own home.
t.1.201.27: Seeing those two great asuras with their boons obtained and their desires fulfilled, all their friends and kinsmen rejoiced along with them.
t.1.201.28: Then the two cast off their matted locks and became crowned, adorned with costly ornaments and wearing spotless garments.
t.1.201.29: And the two lords of the Daityas, supremely delighted, held an untimely Kaumudī festival granting every desire, and so too did their circle of friends.
t.1.201.30: "Let there be eating, let there be feasting, let there be constant delight, let there be singing, let there be drinking, and let there be giving!" Such were the words heard in every house.
t.1.201.32: As those Daityas, who could take any form at will, sported together with these many and various pleasures, the years passed for them as if they were but a single day.
t.1.201.31: Here and there, with great drinking feasts resounding with loud clapping of palms, the whole city of the Daityas became joyful and delighted.
